findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.redbison.dev" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_tools, get_tool, list_calculators, run_calculator, curl_to_code, hmac, redirect_rules, word_count · Private data: search_tools, yaml_to_json, xml_beautify, jwt_decode, hash_compare, password_generate, bcrypt_hash, bcrypt_verify, chmod_convert, docker_run_to_compose, gitignore_generate, js_beautify, json_schema_validate, mime_lookup, nato_phonetic, password_strength, redirect_rules, toml_convert · Public sink: subnet_calculator, random_email, curl_to_code, docker_run_to_compose, hmac, http_status, json_schema_validate, mime_lookup, utm_build, word_count · Destructive: search_tools, json_format, sql_beautify, escape_characters, remove_duplicate_lines, remove_extra_spaces, remove_empty_lines, list_calculators, run_calculator, cron_build, docker_run_to_compose, js_beautify.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
